explainedBy: The everyman clutches the rules he followed, and the excuse 'it's not my fault' is struck out: following the rules no longer clears him.

storyboard.claim: We can no longer hide behind 'I did my job, I followed the rules'; we must look at the whole and restructure the rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman holding his rules on the machine-room stage, the excuse struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the heavier moral burden into the excuse we can no longer use.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the rejected excuse as rejected, not endorsed.

explainedBy: The same everyman now reaches for the giant paradigm lever instead of hiding behind the rules: responsibility means pulling the strongest lever even when it hurts.

storyboard.claim: We are the ones who must reach for the paradigm lever even when it hurts, and stop shouting at the slinky.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman reaching toward the big iron lever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man, same stage: he drops the excuse and reaches for the lever.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lever icon names the strongest leverage point the narration means.

explainedBy: The host beside the slinky dancing from a hand: the opening image returns, now as something to redesign rather than shout at.

storyboard.claim: We have to redesign it, which brings us back to the metal coil dancing in the hand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The slinky hanging from a hand and bouncing, the host beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the lever back to the episode's opening image, the slinky.
storyboard.addedInformation: Brings back the signature slinky the hosts name.

explainedBy: The host points at the bouncing coil, not at the hand: the bounce comes from the slinky's own tension and mass.

storyboard.claim: The slinky bounces not because of the hand but because of what it is: its tension, its mass.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same slinky; the host now points at the coil itself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same slinky; the host shifts from holding to pointing at the coil.
storyboard.addedInformation: Directs the eye from the hand to the coil.

explainedBy: The crash diet tried every January that predictably fails: the dieter slumps over the plate.
noVisual: The crash diet and shifting dominance have no icon; the slinky carries 'its structure' and the callout labels it.

storyboard.claim: Its structure; and we can apply this to our own lives, like the January crash diet that always fails by shifting dominance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The crash diet tried every January that predictably fails: the dieter slumps over the plate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the slinky sequence: the cause is the structure. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the crash-diet example stays in the audio.

explainedBy: The everyman and his spouse argue face to face, both angry, the same fight on repeat like a broken record.

storyboard.claim: The argument with your spouse loops like a broken record, the same lines and resentment every time: the reinforcing loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Husband and wife arguing angrily at home.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second everyday example after the crash diet.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two people locked in the recurring argument.

explainedBy: The tiny control dial alone on screen: yelling at people and twisting small settings is the weak lever the narration tells us to stop using.

storyboard.claim: No matter how often the manager yells, the team still misses deadlines; stop blaming the people, stop twisting the tiny dials.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The control-panel dial with tick marks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Third example (the late team) and the verdict on all three.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dial names the weak lever the narration rejects.

explainedBy: The stressed everyman at work searches with a magnifier beside the clock: look for the delays and the loops of stress, not the culprits.

storyboard.claim: Look at the system: where are the massive delays, where are the reinforcing loops of stress?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried, slumped worker holding a magnifier next to a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From 'stop blaming' to what to look at instead.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock carries the delays, the magnifier the act of looking.

explainedBy: The same everyman, magnifier in hand, finds the target the system is really aiming at: a hidden goal overwriting the stated one.

storyboard.claim: What is the unstated hidden goal of the system that overwrites the stated goal?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman with the magnifier, now facing a target, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man still searching; what he finds changes from delays to the hidden goal.

explainedBy: Donella Meadows holds her finished book: at its very end she admits something humbling.

storyboard.claim: At the end of the book, after all the equations and diagrams, Meadows admits something deeply humbling.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Meadows holding her book in a lecture room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shift from the listener's life to the author's conclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the author on screen with her book.

explainedBy: Meadows, sad, beside the control dial: we cannot perfectly control complex systems.

storyboard.claim: We cannot perfectly control complex systems; they are too messy, nonlinear and interconnected for our bounded brains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Meadows, sad, beside the control dial: we cannot perfectly control complex systems.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same author and book; her face drops with the admission. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the face carries the humility, the callout the claim.

explainedBy: Meadows lifts from sadness into a joyful move: we will never be gods of the system, but we can dance with it.

storyboard.claim: We will never be gods of the system, but we can learn to dance with them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same author; sad face turns into a happy celebration.
storyboard.addedInformation: The change in posture shows the turn from limit to hope.

explainedBy: Meadows, calm and smiling, gives the advice: stay humble and learn the system's beat before trying to force it.
noVisual: Listening to a system has no picture; the author's advice is carried by her and the callout.

storyboard.claim: We can get the beat of the system, stay humble, stay a learner and listen before smashing it into compliance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Meadows speaking warmly in the lecture room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same author; from dancing to the advice itself.

explainedBy: The everyman slumps at home over the recurring problem the hosts ask the viewer to picture.
noVisual: The viewer's own problem is unnamed; the slumped everyman stands in for the listener.

storyboard.claim: Final thought: look at the most frustrating, recurring, intractable problem in your life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped and worried at home.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Meadows back to the listener.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the problem itself stays unnamed, as in the audio.

explainedBy: The same everyman now lies awake in bed, worried: the problem keeps him up at night, and he may blame no one for it.

storyboard.claim: The problem that keeps you up at night; imagine being forbidden from blaming any person for it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman lying awake in bed, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man; from slumped to lying awake.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes 'keeps you up at night' literal.

explainedBy: Three buckets replace the people to blame: an invisible rule, a hidden delay, an underlying structure.

storyboard.claim: Not yourself either: what invisible rule, hidden delay or underlying structure would you be forced to find?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with three buckets: invisible rule, hidden delay, underlying structure.
storyboard.onScreenText: Invisible rule / Hidden delay / Underlying structure
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The answer to the final question: look at the structure, not people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three places to look, from the narration.
